blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Taxes can sound complicated, but in English they follow simple patterns. In this lesson, you learn the words that appear on Czarnikow's forms and reports.

Today you learn five useful words: deadline, payment, date, month, and calendar. You practise them in short, natural sentences. We use the preposition on with days and dates, for example: "The payment is due on Monday" or "The deadline is on the tenth."

Go slowly — one step at a time. Every month, the team checks the tax calendar before the deadline. When you know these words, taxes become easier. English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts. You can do it!

items.q: How many new words does the lesson teach today?
items.why: "Today you learn five useful words: deadline, payment, date, month, and calendar."

items.q: Which preposition do we use with days and dates?
items.why: "We use the preposition on with days and dates" — on Monday, on the tenth.

items.q: When does the team check the tax calendar?
items.why: "Every month, the team checks the tax calendar before the deadline."

items.q: The text says "English comes in CAN's, not in CAN'Ts." This suggests that the author wants you to feel…
items.why: Inferência: a frase é de encorajamento — o autor quer que você se sinta confiante ("You can do it!").

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Taxes follow simple patterns in English.
You should learn one step at a time.
Taxes are too hard to ever understand.
These words appear on real Czarnikow forms.
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo diz que impostos ficam mais fáceis com prática — o autor discorda que sejam impossíveis.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie revisar o calendário fiscal com um colega. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi! Come and sit here. Let's look at the tax calendar for this month together. It's quick, I promise, and it is really not hard.

First, here is the calendar on the wall. I like to mark the important dates in red, so we can see them fast. Look — the first payment is due on Monday. That's the fifth. Please don't forget that date. It is the most important one.

The second payment is on the twentieth. We always send the form two days before the deadline, so we are never late. The accountant reviews the numbers first, then we send it. Two people always check, never just one.

One more thing. On Friday, we check every payment for the month. If something is wrong, we still have time to fix it. That's why we check early, and not on the last day.

Taxes are just one more part of our routine. One small step at a time, okay? You can do this. Next month, you will do the calendar, and I will only watch. Any questions? Great — let's mark these dates now.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Sophie do with the important dates?
items.why: "I like to mark the important dates in red."

items.q: When is the first payment due?
items.why: "the first payment is due on Monday. That's the fifth."

items.q: Why does the team send the form two days before the deadline?
options: Because the accountant is on holiday
items.why: "We always send the form two days before the deadline, so we are never late."

items.q: Why does Sophie check every payment on Friday?
options: So there is still time to fix any mistake
Because the boss asks her to
items.why: Inferência: "If something is wrong, we still have time to fix it. That's why we check early."

items.q: What does Sophie suggest about next month?
options: She will do the calendar alone
The colleague will do the calendar, and she will watch
There will be no tax calendar
items.why: Inferência: "Next month, you will do the calendar, and I will only watch" — ela passa a tarefa ao colega.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The deadline for the tax is next Friday." A deadline is…
options: a final date or time limit
items.why: Deadline = prazo final, a data limite para fazer algo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The company sends the ___ to the government every month."
items.why: Payment = pagamento; é o que a empresa envia ao governo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Please write the correct ___ on the form: the tenth of March."
items.why: Date = data; "the tenth of March" é uma data.

items.q: "We pay this tax every month." A month is…
options: one of the twelve parts of a year
items.why: Month = mês; um ano tem doze meses.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The tax dates are all on the ___ near my desk."
items.why: Calendar = calendário; é onde ficam marcadas as datas.

blocks.instruction: Expressões simples que aparecem em reuniões sobre impostos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager has to sign off on the payment first." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Let's write down the deadline on the calendar." To write down means to…
items.why: Write down = anotar, colocar por escrito.

items.q: "I will follow up with the accountant tomorrow." To follow up means to…
options: check again to make sure it is done
items.why: Follow up = dar continuidade, checar de novo para garantir que foi feito.

items.q: "Don't forget to check off each date when it is paid." To check off means to…
items.why: Check off = marcar como concluído, riscar da lista.

items.q: "We are on time with every payment this month." On time means…
items.why: On time = na hora certa, sem atraso.
